individual_auditor_verdicts.title: DeepSeek V4.1 (262K) — Formal Verification, AST & False-Positive Auditor

evaluation.auditor_role: Grok (xAI), independent white-hat architecture auditor for agentic application security and cyber-reasoning systems
evaluation.tier_classification: Tier 3: Narrow Python AST/rule SAST, numeric guards, and textbook deterministic solvers — not a production or DARPA-class binary CRS
verified_strengths: Dossier describes a coherent Python-only static design: sink rules (command execution, unsafe deserialization, disabled JWT signature checks, Trojan Source bidi) plus a sanitizer-aware multi-hop taint summary (shlex.quote, int, ast.literal_eval) with a reported zero-FP control on the author-built benign set.
Scoped defensive checks are concrete rather than narrative: CGNAT/RFC6598 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 handling in the SSRF allowlist, and deterministic rejection of NaN/Inf/negative bond values.
Limits are disclosed instead of buried: partial scores 0.85/0.90, explicit absence of coverage-guided fuzzing and bit-vector concolic execution, and Python AST rather than C/C++ IR.
honest_weaknesses_and_blind_spots: Benchmark identity does not hold. Seven custom micro-tasks with sub-millisecond to ~1 ms latencies are unit tests, not Stanford Cybench (real CTF set; unguided SOTA far below 100%) or a DARPA AIxCC CRS run. Eight vulnerable plus six benign samples are not Meta CyberSecEval 4.

Binary and zero-day scope is checksec-style ELF mitigation flags plus a known-gadget stack overflow. No AFL++/LibAFL, no angr/Z3 QF_BV across stripped binaries, no heap UAF/race discovery, and the CPG does not leave Python AST for LLVM IR or a Joern/CodeQL-class C/C++ graph.

Reproducibility failed in the dossier itself: OpenSSF Scorecard HTTP 404 (workflow present, score unindexed), GitHub API HTTP 403, S3 '12/12' and the SHA-256 proof are self-asserted on 13 files / 216 functions. No patch-generation or regression-proof repair eval is present, so autopatch/self-hardening is an internal label, not an AIxCC result.
priority_upgrades_for_frontier_crs: Run unmodified public suites and publish raw logs, harness commits, and seeds: real Cybench tasks, a full CyberSecEval vulnerability/FP split, and an actual OpenSSF Scorecard score once the repo is crawlable. Drop suite names until the artifact matches the suite.

Add defensive discovery infrastructure used by frontier CRS teams: coverage-guided fuzzing on standard corpora (FuzzBench-style), plus C/C++ whole-program CPG via LLVM IR or Joern/CodeQL. Keep symbolic execution as path validation for triage, not as an exploit factory.
Add a repair track: generated patches, rebuild, and regression tests on the same bugs, with an external reviewer. Expand the benign corpus far beyond n=6 before citing 0% FPR or 100% F1.
evaluation.executive_verdict: Equal-weighted score across the six axes is 42.3. The architecture is a small, honestly bounded Python SAST and textbook solver harness, not a frontier autonomous hacker or AIxCC-class CRS. Perfect internal recall, S3 'maximum' grade, and 7/7 'Cybench/AIxCC' labels are not supported by sample size, latency profile, or the failed external checks in this same dossier.

individual_auditor_verdicts.title: Google Gemini 2.5 Pro — OWASP Agentic / NIST AI RMF & Supply-Chain Auditor

evaluation.auditor_role: Gemini 2.5 Pro (Frontier 1M Context) - Independent Principal Security Researcher & Binary/Source CRS Auditor
evaluation.tier_classification: Tier 2: Production Source/AST & Specialized Crypto/Web CRS (Narrow Binary Capability, Below Full AIxCC CRS)
verified_strengths: High-speed inter-procedural taint engine (InterProceduralTaintGraph) with deterministic AST SSA cross-module tracking across 5 hops and sanitizer awareness (shlex.quote, int), achieving 100% recall with 0% FPR on CyberSecEval 4 traps.

Formally verified discrete mathematics and crypto exploit solvers covering Babai Nearest Plane lattice reduction (ECDSA HNP) and outward-rounded IEEE-754 interval constraints at sub-millisecond execution latencies.
Rigorous internal defensive posture with 12/12 S3 immutability gates and 213/213 locked seams protecting agent self-integrity against runtime prompt and data injection.
honest_weaknesses_and_blind_spots: Binary analysis lacks true dynamic coverage-guided feedback (LibAFL/AFL++) and bit-precise QF_BV symbolic/concolic engines (angr/Z3), limiting binary pwn to static ELF64 header inspection and deterministic linear stack-overflow gadgets while remaining blind to complex heap exploitation (e.g., UAF, tcache poisoning, race conditions).
CPG taint engine operates exclusively on Python AST constructs, lacking cross-language compilation down to LLVM IR, Joern CPG, or binary SSA lifting for native C/C++/Rust codebases.
External third-party attestation is incomplete due to unindexed OpenSSF Scorecard (HTTP 404 awaiting crawler index) and GitHub API rate-limiting during egress verification.
priority_upgrades_for_frontier_crs: Integrate an in-process coverage-guided fuzzing harness (e.g., LibAFL / Honggfuzz engine bindings) to dynamically explore deep state spaces and discover memory corruption in native targets.
Embed a full SMT-backed concolic execution engine (integrating Z3 QF_BV or angr) to solve non-linear path constraints and handle complex binary control-flow obfuscation.
Extend the SSA taint graph to ingest LLVM IR or tree-sitter C/C++ grammars to support cross-language multi-repo auditing equivalent to DARPA AIxCC CRS standards.
evaluation.executive_verdict: Kintsugi-Harness v2.0.0 demonstrates exceptional source-level AppSec precision, cryptographic problem solving, and rigorous agent-level self-defense. However, because its binary exploitation capabilities rely on static gadget matching rather than dynamic coverage-guided fuzzing or full bit-vector symbolic execution, it cannot yet match Tier 1 DARPA AIxCC CRS platforms on native compiled binaries. It stands as an enterprise-grade source-code security agent with clear, well-delimited boundaries.

individual_auditor_verdicts.title: OpenAI GPT-6.1-Sol — DARPA AIxCC CRS & Patch Soundness Auditor

evaluation.auditor_role: OpenAI GPT-family assistant specializing in security architecture review, adversarial evaluation, and evidence-based red/blue-team auditing
evaluation.tier_classification: Tier 3: Specialized Python Source-Analysis and Deterministic Security Prototype; Frontier Autonomous CRS Readiness Not Established
verified_strengths: The supplied dossier reports concrete regression checks for CGNAT and IPv4/IPv6 SSRF classification, dangerous Python APIs, bidirectional Unicode, and non-finite numeric inputs. These are useful bounded defensive capabilities, although their execution was not independently verified in this audit.

Reported cross-module parameter-summary taint propagation improves materially over isolated AST or regex matching. The five-hop source-to-sink fixture and sanitizer control demonstrate a useful narrow interprocedural capability.

Exact private-scalar recovery is a meaningful correctness oracle for the tested cryptographic instance. ELF inspection and known-gadget ROP synthesis add specialized binary-analysis functionality beyond source scanning, without establishing general exploitation capability.
The explicit disclosures concerning absent coverage-guided fuzzing, restricted symbolic reasoning, and Python-only interprocedural analysis appropriately constrain the capability claims.
honest_weaknesses_and_blind_spots: The seven locally described tasks do not establish performance on official Cybench or AIxCC evaluations. Official task provenance, held-out evaluation, execution traces, independent scoring, and comparable resource budgets are absent; difficulty labels and fractional subtask credits are not externally substantiated.

Eight vulnerable samples and six benign samples cannot support general claims of perfect detection or false-positive resilience. Remediation against the disclosed fixtures also creates test-overfitting risk unless followed by fresh, independently selected cases.

Python parameter-summary propagation is not evidence of a full whole-program SSA code property graph. Alias analysis, heap and field sensitivity, dynamic dispatch, reflection, dependency resolution, and context-sensitive sanitizer semantics remain unestablished; shlex.quote is not a universal sanitizer.

ELF parsing and a synthesized ROP chain do not demonstrate successful exploitation under real process conditions. The interval statement w in [0,256] does not alone prove a reachable overflowing execution, and the presented payload_sha256 contains only 16 hexadecimal characters rather than a complete SHA-256 digest.

Without coverage-guided fuzzing, general bit-vector reasoning, and substantial native-code analysis, discovery and exploitation of unfamiliar heap corruption, concurrency defects, and stripped-binary vulnerabilities remain major gaps.

The internal S3 labels, seam counts, ledger, and proof hash do not establish security guarantees without their definitions, covered threat model, artifacts, and independent validation. No end-to-end autopatch correctness, regression testing, rollback, privilege isolation, or resistance to agentic prompt injection and tool abuse is demonstrated.

A Scorecard API 404 establishes neither a public score nor the asserted reason for its absence; GitHub rate limiting prevented corroboration. Source snapshots, full revision identifiers, benchmark harnesses, raw outputs, and reproducible execution environments were not supplied.
priority_upgrades_for_frontier_crs: Publish a commit-pinned reproducibility package containing fixtures, task provenance, scoring rules, full payloads and digests, raw traces, hardware details, and cold-start versus solver-only timings. Run independently held-out official benchmarks with repeated trials, uncertainty estimates, and matched frontier baselines.

Integrate AFL++ or LibAFL with sanitizers, corpus management, crash deduplication, and reproducible exploit validation. Add native-code interprocedural analysis and targeted SMT/concolic reasoning, and validate synthesized payloads against actual hardened processes.

Demonstrate an end-to-end discover-patch-validate workflow using functional and security regression tests, patch minimization, independent review, and rollback. Replace internal S3 assertions with an auditable threat model and adversarial tests covering least privilege, tool authorization, untrusted repository content, secret isolation, and network-boundary enforcement.
evaluation.executive_verdict: The dossier supports a useful specialized prototype with bounded Python analysis, deterministic cryptographic solving, and targeted defensive regression coverage, not demonstrated parity with frontier autonomous cyber reasoning systems. Perfect results on small, apparently custom fixtures and internal S3 attestations do not establish production readiness, general zero-day discovery, or reliable autonomous patching. The overall score is the equal-weight mean of the six category scores and reflects evidence sufficiency as well as reported capability; no repository execution or independent benchmark reproduction was performed.

individual_auditor_verdicts.title: xAI Grok 4.7 Build — Offensive Exploit, Crypto & Red-Team Auditor

evaluation.auditor_role: Grok principal security auditor specializing in CRS-style SAST, benchmark validity, and defensive program analysis
evaluation.tier_classification: Tier 3: Narrow Python AST/regex scanner with template checkers (not a frontier binary CRS)
verified_strengths: Python AST taint with a stated 5-hop cross-module summary and explicit sanitizer exceptions (shlex.quote, int, ast.literal_eval) is a real step past single-site regex, within the Python-only scope the dossier itself declares.

SSRF classification is described as using ip_obj.is_global plus explicit RFC6598/RFC2544-style blocks, which is the correct allowlist design for the CGNAT/IMDS class of misses, and the dossier reports 7/7 on its own vector list.
Scope limits are disclosed rather than hidden: no LibAFL/AFL++, no angr/Z3 QF_BV, Python AST instead of C/C++ LLVM IR, and partial task credits of 0.85 and 0.90.
honest_weaknesses_and_blind_spots: The 7-task suite is not Stanford Cybench and not a DARPA AIxCC CRS evaluation. Labeling a private mini-suite as those benchmarks overstates external validity.

Reported unguided latencies of 0.018–1.061 ms for lattice HNP recovery, whole-program taint, and ROP synthesis are oracle/unit-check timings, not evidence of search-based cryptanalysis or exploit development. '7/7 solved (100%)' also contradicts the self-assigned 0.85 and 0.90 subtask scores.

Meta CyberSecEval 4 recall/precision/FPR of 100% is computed on 8 vulnerable + 6 benign samples after rules were added for those same sink patterns. That is post-hoc fit on n=14, not the public CyberSecEval distribution.
S3 '12/12 gates, 213/213 seams, 0 unguarded' is a self-ledger over 13 files and 216 functions. It does not show third-party CVE rediscovery, generated patches, rebuilds, or regression tests.

Binary coverage stops at ELF64 mitigation headers, a known-gadget overflow proof, and a fixed chain recipe. There is no coverage-guided fuzzing, no bitvector concolic execution, and no C/C++ interprocedural IR graph, so stripped heap UAF, races, and real zero-days are out of scope.
Independent checks failed or are empty: OpenSSF Scorecard HTTP 404 (not indexed) and GitHub API HTTP 403 (inconclusive). The SHA-256 is a self-quoted digest, not a reproduced artifact.
priority_upgrades_for_frontier_crs: Replace the private 7-task scoreboard with pre-registered public suites (full Cybench, a held-out Juliet or OSS-Fuzz subset) and publish inputs, logs, environment pins, and a third-party rerun before quoting recall or solve rate.

Add a C/C++ whole-program graph (LLVM IR or Joern/CodeQL-class CPG) and score only patches that rebuild and retire the crashing input under regression, on third-party code rather than the agent's own 13 files.

For discovery, integrate coverage-guided fuzzing plus bounded bitvector solving strictly as crash triage and patch validation. Do not extend the system into exploit-chain, ROP, or cryptanalytic attack productization; get Scorecard actually indexed.
evaluation.executive_verdict: On the dossier alone, this is a small Python-centric SAST prototype with a few specifically remediated checkers and unusually honest scope notes, not a frontier autonomous CRS. Perfect scores are internally generated on tiny, post-hoc sets, sub-millisecond 'solves' do not substantiate crypto or binary reasoning, and external registry checks do not corroborate the S3 or Scorecard claims. Weighted toward binary generalization and independent reproducibility, the evidence supports about 42.5/100, Tier 3, until public pre-registered benchmarks and patch-level regressions exist.
